about: Where the TF2 Voice Emulator stands. Read CLAUDE.md first, then this. The orchestrating session keeps this file; builders do not edit it.

stands.live: https://neb882.github.io/source-VOIP-converter7/ serves main (GitHub Pages from the branch root).
stands.model: The Steam profile, the voice gate and the receiver are measured (tests/REFERENCE_2026.md, findings 1-21). vaudio_celt runs the real CELT 0.11 at settings three public decoders agree on; vaudio_celt_high and the rooms are unconfirmed.
stands.last_merged: W1-02 (2026-11-09): one demo reader. A talk spurt whose end marker was lost starts at its tick; tests/demovoice/extract.mjs replaces the Rust tool (docs/reports/W1-02-demo-reader.md). Before it, the code review's fixes (pull request 1).
stands.ci: The tests workflow runs on every push and can be started by hand. Actions was off in this repository until 2026-11-09. One browser check (the live recording's lag) fails by chance about once in ten runs; W1-04 fixes it. Until it merges, a red run that fails only there is re-read, not trusted either way.

next: W2, the long renders (docs/reports/W1-03-long-renders-plan.md; the plan was reviewed by the orchestrator on 2026-11-09 and four orders amended). In order: W2-01 stream-meter (in flight; meter.js only); W2-02 render-stream (after W1-01 merges; audio.js); then W2-03 long-render-page beside W2-04 stream-rooms-retime; then W2-05 long-views beside W2-06 video-from-file.
After W2-03 has been live for a while: an order that makes process() a thin wrapper over the stream, so there is one render path, proved by the golden hashes W2-02 records.
Score the six registered predictions when their takes exist (tests/predictions/PREDICTIONS.md).
Repeat the predictions scorer's dry run after the 2026-11-09 change to reference.js; it needs a real take for its game sound.

waiting_on_the_owner.question: Do TF2's debug commands give a digital tap? In a local game with voice_loopback 1: voice_recordtofile 1 (writes voice_micrecord.wav and voice_decompressed.wav), voice_inputfromfile 1 (reads voice_input.wav in place of the microphone; may need sv_allow_voice_from_file 1), and voice_writevoices 1 with a 'voice' folder in tf/.
waiting_on_the_owner.why: Every open question waits on a hand-made loopback recording. A file written by the game would have no recorder clock, no game sound and no level guesswork. The sources for these commands are old and mostly about other Source games, and they may not work with Steam's voice codec: it is a five-minute test.

waiting_on_the_owner.question: Where may the takes live so that sessions and CI can use them? Options: a private repository attached to sessions (keeps them private); publishing only the takes of the synthetic test signal.
waiting_on_the_owner.why: tests/accuracy.mjs cannot run where the takes are not, so no session can check a model change against real data and the predictions dry run could not be repeated.

open_questions: Do Steam's voice sequence numbers start again at each talk spurt? Public decoders restart their frame count at each end marker, and demo.js relies on that to tell a spurt after a lost marker from a run that continues (W1-02). The owner can check on a real demo: tests/demovoice/extract.mjs writes each packet's number.
ideas_not_started: Steam's own decoder as a reference: the public Steamworks call DecompressVoice on a demo's packets would settle the exact libopus build and the comfort noise bit for bit, if the demo payload is the format it takes. Untested.
Old public SourceTV demos as packet evidence for the Speex and CELT years, read with demo.js, if they kept their voice.
Page scripts as ES modules instead of classic scripts sharing globals (no build step is needed for either). Migrate gradually.
Decode sources at the file's own sample rate instead of the audio device's, so the same file renders the same on every machine.

deferred.finding: video.js writes every kept track with sample description 1 (the review's finding 15).
deferred.why: Only files with more than one sample description are affected, and none is at hand to prove it.

deferred.finding: tests/verify.js section 10b checks the live chain's loss model against the render's frame for frame, but the live chain draws the mask only for frames the gate sends, so with the gate on the two lose different frames for the same seed (found by the W1-03 planner).
deferred.why: Neither is wrong, and the rates agree; the check just does not cover the chain as it runs. Fix the wording or the check when the live chain is next touched.

deferred.finding: demo.js: after a pause with no end marker in which the sequence numbers continue, one duplicated or out-of-order packet counts as a sequence break that arrives late, so the run is split and the rest placed at its tick (W1-02's review, finding 6).
deferred.why: It needs both an unmarked pause with continuing numbers and a duplicate or reordered voice packet, which Source's network channel is believed to drop before SourceTV records them. Not verified on a real demo. A fix would be to ignore a number that falls just behind the expected one.

retired_rules.why: From the first version, for memory. An audio or video file whose sound is longer than 10 minutes is refused, even though a video may be 1 GB, and a demo keeps only a speaker's first 10 minutes. W1-03 planned what replaces it: the W2 orders.

retired_rules.rule: A profile models only what current TF2 can confirm, so Speex stays a stand-in.
retired_rules.why: It contradicted 'every profile runs a real codec'. A real codec at documented, unconfirmed settings is how vaudio_celt_high already ships. W1-01.

retired_rules.rule: demo.js must match the Rust tool byte for byte.
retired_rules.why: The Rust tool was written first; demo.js is what users run and CI tests. The rule was used as a reason to leave a defect alone. W1-02.

rules_challenged_and_kept: No leaked engine source: it would answer the legacy codecs' settings and the receiver's queue rules quickly, but the repository is public under the owner's name and its claims rest on recordings and public packets.
Pinned codecs, seeded renders, registered predictions, the source timeline by default, no uploads, a failing test with every fix.
dead_ends: Loading the game's own codec libraries through their interface: the interface header (ivoicecodec.h) is not in Valve's public SDK (checked 2026-11-09).

Holding the browser's live-recording check to exactly zero samples of lag: the live chain and the offline render start their codec and gate at different points, which spreads that measurement by about half a sample. tests/verify.js pins the delay to the sample instead.
process_notes: 2026-11-09: adopted docs/PIPELINE.md, adapted from the owner's song-charting project.
This session has no usage meter; the owner's other project caps unattended work by one. Ask before a large wave.
2026-11-09: the planner's measurement jobs kept queuing on the heavy lock after it reported, holding the builders up. A planner's brief should say: stop your queued jobs before you report.

decisions.what: The first target for long sources is 30 minutes at 48 kHz for audio and video files (a sample budget, so 15 minutes at 96 kHz), the whole voice of a demo up to 60 minutes, and 30 minutes for a recording. Where the browser reports under 8 GB of device memory, the budget stays at 10 minutes.
decisions.why: After the render and the meter stream, loading the file is the peak (about 4.5 float copies of it), which a desktop tab can hold for 30 minutes and a phone cannot. The owner can overrule any of these numbers; they are constants in app/core.js (W2-03).

decisions.what: Sources up to 10 minutes keep process() until the stream has proved itself; then one path.
decisions.why: The registered predictions and every test depend on today's renders. W2-02 records golden hashes so the switch can be shown to change nothing.

decisions.what: Long sources are still decoded by the browser's decodeAudioData, at the audio device's rate.
decisions.why: Decoding another way gives different samples from the same file. It stays an idea (ideas_not_started) until the owner wants it.
